Comber AOI WebGIS — 2002 vs 2008 Earth Observation

Newtownards Road, Comber, Co. Down, BT23 5ZP · Strangford Lough · what3words ///magnetic.deeply.orbited
NOT an investigation conclusion. This is a geospatial data viewer. Imagery is satellite-resolution (Landsat 30 m / MODIS 250 m); a 1–2 m buried object is sub-pixel and cannot be located here. The change layers are quantitative pixel computations, not visual interpretation. No determination about burial, concealment, or intent is made. Drum-scale (~0.25–1 m) evidence requires commercial air photos (see Limitations).
Toggle years / layers top-right. Base = Esri World Imagery. Orange dot = site point; circle = ~250 m buffer; red squares = top 2002→2008 change blocks. Imagery is georeferenced to its true bounds (inlined, no external dependencies).

2 · What you are looking at

Every image is genuine retrieved data (Planetary Computer STAC / NASA GIBS), georeferenced and overlaid on its true bounds. The 2002, 2005 and 2008 Landsat crops are pixel-co-registered (identical bounding box), so toggling is a like-for-like comparison. The red squares mark the 16×16 px blocks with the largest local luminance change 2002→2008. They cluster along the north-west shoreline / estuary margin — consistent with tidal / vegetation change, not a discrete object.

Block centres (~250 m at 30 m GSD). Coarse land-cover / shoreline change hotspots for review — not a location.

4 · Limitations

  • Resolution. Landsat 30 m / MODIS 250 m cannot resolve a drum. Change layers show large-area change only.
  • Drum-scale = commercial. Only ~0.25–1 m 2002–2008 coverage is order-only air photography: OSNI / Land & Property Services (start here), Bluesky, Getmapping, NCAP. Not freely downloadable.
  • No visual verification. Change layers are computed from decoded pixels; confirm visually with a human.
  • No determination. Nothing here infers burial, concealment, or intent.
